title: The Melted Candy Bar That Invented the Microwave
topic: Percy Spencer, 1945: a candy bar melts in his pocket next to a radar magnetron; popcorn, an egg, and the first microwave oven
mechanism: A radar magnetron sends out microwaves that make the water in food twist back and forth; the friction between molecules is heat, so food cooks with no flame, and a self-taught radar engineer turned that into the microwave oven.

beats.hook: The story goes: a candy bar melted in an engineer's pocket, and nothing in the room was hot. The camera pushes along a radar bench past a humming MAGNETRON onto Spencer's coat pocket oozing chocolate.
beats.but: He was Percy Spencer, who never finished grammar school and taught himself the science; in the war his method built 2,600 magnetrons a day.
beats.then: He tests it: raw popcorn kernels held by the tube pop all over the lab.
beats.conflict: Next an egg: it shakes and bursts across the bench, a colleague flinches: 'Percy!'
beats.pivot: You see, the tube sends out microwaves; they make the water in food twist back and forth, and that rubbing is heat, right inside the food. No flame at all.
beats.so: So a patent was filed on 8 October 1945, and the first oven of 1947 stood six feet tall and weighed 750 pounds; twenty years later, in 1967, a countertop model cost 495 dollars.
beats.closing: Every bag of microwave popcorn goes back to one melted candy bar.

triple_hook.visual: Chocolate already dripping from the pocket of Spencer's suit jacket in a thick brown string, beside a glowing copper MAGNETRON tube that hums and flickers; the camera is already pushing in.
triple_hook.verbal: The story goes, this man's candy bar melted in his pocket, and nothing in the room was hot.

format_note: The magnetron, the candy bar, the popcorn kernels and the water molecule model are drawn about 2x real size so they read on a phone. The candy bar has a plain paper wrapper with no brand.
